presets.name: Name
presets.name_hint: Shown on the button; leave empty to show the start of the instructions

make_video.name: Make the video
make_video.prompt: Make a video from this piece: portrait or landscape for the platforms it goes to (9:16 for Douyin and Xiaohongshu, 16:9 for YouTube and Bilibili), about 60 seconds. Say what it's about in the first 3 seconds, follow the structure of the draft (or the content if there's no draft), get the key points across in voice-over or captions, and end with a line inviting people to follow. Also write the video's title, description and tags.

from_draft.name: Write from the draft
from_draft.prompt: Write the text to post from this piece's draft: title, body (the description for videos) and tags, following my writing instructions. Keep the draft's points, examples and wording where you can, fill in the structure, and don't invent anything that isn't in the draft.

post_images.name: Make 5 images
post_images.prompt: Make 5 images for this piece: 3:4 portrait; the first is the cover (a big headline that says what it's about at a glance), the rest each cover one point with little, large text and a consistent palette.

cover.name: Make a cover
cover.prompt: Make a cover image for this piece: a big headline that says what it's about at a glance, 3:4 portrait for posts and 16:9 landscape for long-form, simple style.

to_video.name: Make it a video
to_video.prompt: Write a new video piece: write the video's title, description and tags, then make the video itself (as in "Work on this": about 60 seconds, portrait or landscape for the platforms, say what it's about in the first 3 seconds).

keywords.title: Keyword opportunities
keywords.desc: Find what buyers search from your product terms; the assistant reviews and groups them, and they're sorted by Google ranking into things to do: improve existing pages or write new content. Work in progress sits under "Working on" to see if rankings rise.
keywords.launch_desc: Hand it to the assistant: it uses your profile and products as seeds for autocomplete, adds queries your site already shows for on Google, drops irrelevant ones, tags search intent, groups them into topics and saves them here. You can follow along in the chat on the right.
keywords.req_hint: Target market, which keywords you want or don't, modifiers. Every run follows this after you change it.
keywords.no_gsc: This site isn't linked to Search Console: you can find and review keywords, but there is no ranking data to spot quick wins. Link it on the Google rankings page and they update automatically.
keywords.raw_left: {n} keywords not reviewed yet. Click "Find keywords" and the assistant continues.
keywords.empty: No keywords yet. Click "Find keywords" and the assistant will collect a batch from your products, review them and group them into topics.
keywords.filter_empty: Nothing in this group right now.
keywords.tab_fix_hint: Your site already ranks 4–30 for these, or the page title / H1 doesn't use the keyword: adding content or fixing the title pays off fastest. Page issues are fixed in Site audit.
keywords.tab_write_hint: Keywords you don't rank for yet but can win: Google's top 10 has forum, social or B2B listing pages, or competitors rank. Turn a topic into a content idea.
keywords.tab_doing_hint: Keywords turned into topics or whose page was improved: rankings update weekly, and 17 days after going live they're compared before and after.
keywords.tab_other_hint: Already top 3, dominated by big sites, not checked on Google yet, or dismissed. No need to look often.
keywords.r_missing: page's main keyword, missing from title or H1
keywords.r_open: {n} forum, social or B2B pages in top 10
keywords.r_topic: turned into a topic, waiting to be published
keywords.oh_fix: Have the assistant rewrite title & description
keywords.oh_intro: Checks whether "{kw}" appears in these places on the target page {page}. Google mostly reads the title and H1 to understand what a page is about; the description is the two lines under the title in search results and affects whether people click.
keywords.oh_title_why: The text on the browser tab and the big blue line in search results. Most important: Google and buyers read it first.
keywords.oh_h1_why: The big heading at the top of the page body. Tells Google and readers what the page is about; best kept in line with the title.
keywords.oh_desc_why: The two lines under the title in search results. Doesn't directly affect ranking, but using the keyword and saying what's offered gets more clicks.
keywords.oh_url_why: Having the keyword in the URL helps a little, but isn't worth changing the URL (that needs a redirect and old rankings dip first).
keywords.oh_primary: This is the page's main keyword (the one with the most impressions on this page). When it's missing from the title or H1, Site audit reports it: work it in naturally without stuffing — one or two main keywords per title is enough.
keywords.oh_not_primary: This page's main keyword is a different one, so this is just for reference, not an issue: a title only fits one or two main keywords. To rank for this one, cover it in a section of the body, or write a separate page.
keywords.oh_rule: How it's judged: ignoring small words like for, the, vs, every word must appear (plurals and order don't matter); Chinese terms must appear as a whole. Checked {t} (Site audit checks weekly).

aeo.title: AI citation score
aeo.all_good: Easy for AI to read and quote
aeo.hint: How easily AI can read this article and quote it word for word. Rule-based (no AI model): every item is a fact counted from the body, and the score adds them up. A high score doesn't mean AI will recommend you; that's what the AI search checks measure.
aeo.fix_intro: Improve this article for the AI citation score (now grade {grade}, {score}).
aeo.fix_paras: Weakest paragraphs (counting paragraphs, lists and tables, not headings): {list}.
aeo.fix_rule: Change only these, leave other paragraphs as they are. Use only data, models and certifications from the product catalog and company files; if they aren't there, leave them out. Never invent anything or add unrelated links for the score. Run aeo.article again when done.
aeo.publish_low: AI will find this article hard to read and quote. Close this to see what lost points and ask AI to fix it, or publish anyway.

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.making_desc: AI is making it on this computer; it shows up in this piece's artifacts when done. Click "View" to watch what it is doing.
artifacts.continue_hint: To change it, say so in the chat that made it. Each change is saved as a new artifact; old ones stay.
artifacts.ask_new: Change it in a new chat
artifacts.ask_new_hint: The chat that made it is gone: start a new one and say what to change. Each change is saved as a new artifact.
artifacts.ask_new_text: I want to keep changing the artifacts of {ref} ("{title}"). Follow step 5 of the project task tasks/work-on-article.md: look at its artifacts and notes, then ask me what to change.
artifacts.note_ph: What this is and what changed from the previous one
artifacts.del_in_use: The one used for publishing can't be deleted: pick another one first

playbook.title: Playbook
playbook.empty: Turn this creator's style into a playbook: title formulas, hooks, structure, tone and visuals. Then suggest topics or write posts that follow it. Collect a few of their posts below (with text or screenshots) first.
playbook.analyze_desc: The assistant reads this creator's posts in your library and extracts title formulas, hooks, structure, tone and visuals into a playbook (updating the existing one). It learns the style only, never their facts.
playbook.req_hint: Default instructions for style analysis: which aspects and how detailed.
playbook.topics_desc: Suggest topics that fit this playbook, using its title formulas and your product facts. Writing these topics later follows the playbook automatically.
playbook.write_desc: Write a post following this playbook's structure, titles, hooks and tone. Describe what to write below (topic, points or a draft); leave it empty to pick from the topic pool.
playbook.guide: Writing guide (given to the writing AI)
playbook.new_sources: {n} new posts came in after this analysis. Re-analyze to keep the playbook current.
